title: Novel Glitazones Protect Rotenone-induced Parkinsonism in Mouse Models by Targeting PGC1alpha.
authors: Ayachit, Shreyas; Ramesha, Ganavi Bethanagere; Krishna, Kamsagara Linganna; Pesaladinne, Ujwal Reddy; Ravanappa, Prashanthakumar Bommenahalli; Babu, Divya Durai; Mehdi, Seema; Pathak, Suman
one_liner_zh: 该研究聚焦新型格列酮类化合物对帕金森病小鼠模型的神经保护作用，虽用分子对接和MD评估与PGC-1alpha蛋白结合，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a persistent neurodegenerative condition marked by rising global rates of disability and mortality, warranting the need for new treatment options. The present investigation evaluated the protective effects of novel glitazones C7 and C25 against rotenone-induced PD in a mouse model. METHODS: Molecular docking using Discovery Studio and molecular dynamics simulations were employed to evaluate the binding ability of C7 and C25 to the PGC-1alpha target protein. Pharmacokinetic evaluations of C7 and C25 were performed against the standard pioglitazone in the rats model, and acute toxicity assessments were conducted following OECD guidelines 423. The neuroprotective effects of C7 were tested in a rotenone-induced mouse model of PD at doses of 10, 20, and 30 mg/kg body weight. Behavioral studies, including locomotor activity, grip strength, and catalepsy, as well as biochemical analyses such as endogenous antioxidant levels and AChE levels, were assessed. RESULTS: The novel compound C7 demonstrated good binding and simulation at the PGC-1alpha target protein. The kinetic profile of C7 was found to be good when compared to C25. Both the novel glitazones were safe at 300 mg/kg body weight when tested for oral acute toxicity. The novel compound C7 effectively alleviated symptoms related to rotenone-induced PD, demonstrating its promise as a therapeutic candidate. DISCUSSION: In the rotenone-induced mouse model, compound C7 exhibited a promising anti-PD effect by attenuating oxidative stress and increasing muscular activity, which merits further investigations. CONCLUSION: Additional research using various induction models, along with further investigation of cellular and molecular markers in larger animal studies, is needed to validate these findings.
abstract_zh: 引言：帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）是一种持续性的神经退行性疾病，其全球致残率和死亡率不断上升，亟需新的治疗选择。本研究评估了新型格列酮类化合物C7和C25在鱼藤酮诱导的PD小鼠模型中的保护作用。方法：采用Discovery Studio进行分子对接和分子动力学模拟，评估C7和C25与PGC-1α靶蛋白的结合能力。在大鼠模型中，对C7和C25进行了药代动力学评估，并与标准药物吡格列酮进行比较；急性毒性评估遵循OECD指南423进行。在鱼藤酮诱导的PD小鼠模型中，以10、20和30 mg/kg体重的剂量测试了C7的神经保护作用。行为学研究包括运动活性、握力和僵住症，以及生化分析如内源性抗氧化剂水平和乙酰胆碱酯酶（AChE）水平。结果：新型化合物C7在PGC-1α靶蛋白上表现出良好的结合和模拟效果。与C25相比，C7的药代动力学特征良好。两种新型格列酮类化合物在300 mg/kg体重口服急性毒性测试中均安全。新型化合物C7有效缓解了鱼藤酮诱导的PD相关症状，显示出其作为治疗候选药物的潜力。讨论：在鱼藤酮诱导的小鼠模型中，化合物C7通过减轻氧化应激和增强肌肉活动表现出有前景的抗PD效果，值得进一步研究。结论：需要采用多种诱导模型进行额外研究，并在更大规模的动物研究中进一步探讨细胞和分子标志物，以验证这些发现。
